sources.entry: Deckle - Subtle paper-grain texture overlay for the whole screen. Click-through menu bar app with 18 textures, global hotkey, and per-display control.

summary.one_liner: Deckle is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that overlays a click-through paper-grain texture across the whole screen.
summary.what_it_does: Deckle draws a matte paper texture over every display, with 26 built-in papers and a Paper Mill editor that previews custom papers on the live desktop before saving them. Intensity (5–45%), grain size, grain visibility and matte finish are adjustable, and desk setups save up to eight named combinations. Per-app rules can show the paper everywhere, hide it while chosen apps are frontmost, or show it only for chosen apps. A global hotkey (⌥⌘P) toggles it, and deckle:// URL commands let Shortcuts, Raycast, Alfred, cron or Terminal control it. Opt-in desktop pets (Miso the cat and Tide the fish) animate in a separate small window.
use_cases: reduce screen glare during long reading sessions
give a screen a paper-like texture for writing
toggle a screen overlay from a keyboard shortcut
schedule or automate an overlay with Shortcuts or cron
save and switch between display looks per desk setup
create and share custom paper textures
notable: Click-through, borderless overlay window per display that does not capture mouse input
Spectral fiber (v4) renderer that synthesizes seamless paper grain with Accelerate/vDSP
Paper Mill live preview with contrast and blue-channel estimates
Opt-in desktop pets that need no extra permissions
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later; the Shortcuts time-based automation example needs macOS 26 or later
Not a calibrated blue-light filter; the README makes no medical or clinical claims
Screen-capture hiding is not guaranteed, so some screen-sharing or recording apps may still capture the texture
Homebrew cask can lag behind the latest release; in-app update requires a writable install folder and Developer ID signature
